gaps.construct: with self._condition: (lock held for the block)
gaps.description: The doc has no lock or condition type and says locks are unnecessary. `hold guard as acquire ...` borrows the resource block, but `hold` is defined only for opening resources.
Structured concurrency (`together`) cannot have one task wait on a signal sent by another. There is no wait or notify.

gaps.construct: a Future object mutated by one thread while others hold references to it
gaps.description: `editable` means exclusive ownership, and example 38 forbids shared mutable values between tasks. A Future exists to be shared, so the core purpose of the type is ruled out.

gaps.construct: waiter.add_result(self) over waiters of different classes
gaps.description: There is no interface, trait or method declaration, so dispatch on the run-time kind of waiter has no spelling.
There is no type for a list of stored operations, and a `uses` line cannot say 'whatever these callbacks use'.

gaps.construct: result can be any Python object
gaps.description: There is no 'any' type, and no type parameter can be declared on an operation, so Value is undeclared.
`fail with` shows only bare failure names. Attaching a formatted message, or a payload, is not shown, and there is no repr.

gaps.construct: for waiter in self._waiters: waiter.add_result(self) (changing each element)
gaps.description: Whether a `for each` loop variable may be changed through the list is not covered.

gaps.construct: uses for code that calls user callbacks
gaps.description: The effects of stored callbacks are unknown when the code is written. The doc gives no way to name them.

gaps.construct: 'Should only be used by Executor implementations and unit tests'
gaps.description: There is no visibility or friend construct to say which callers may use an operation. It is kept as a note only.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one.
Structured concurrency only. A task cannot outlive its scope. (A Future is handed to a worker thread that outlives the call that created it.)
invented_syntax: hold guard as acquire condition of future (hold used for a lock)
Waiter used as an interface type
List of Operation taking a Future (function type)
uses condition of future, callbacks of future (capabilities named by field access)
notes: A Future is a shared, thread-safe rendezvous object, which is exactly what Scribe's concurrency model rules out. Translating it is not a matter of syntax: the design needs either a sanctioned shared-cell or channel primitive with a lock, or a statement that futures are replaced by `together` and that thread-pool executors are a non-goal. Lock-scoped blocks would fit naturally as a `hold` form if locks are admitted.
